edge_explainer: Every trap the UK battery was built to catch comes back CLEAN on this name, and that is precisely why there is no edge left. Pension (AR2026 Note 5): two DB schemes closed since 2009 with a GBP 11,999k surplus that is FULLY UNRECOGNISED under IFRIC 14 - the asset ceiling writes it to nil because the group has no unconditional right to refunds under the scheme rules - so book equity of GBP 127.272M contains zero pension surplus and P/B 1.03x is honest. This is the exact opposite of the Churchill China / Costain failure mode. The scheme was bought in with Aviva on 24 March 2020, fully matching liabilities except GMP equalisation; management lists 'buy-in to buy-out' as an opportunity, which is the only path by which the surplus reaches shareholders. Capital commitments (Note 7) are GBP 1,309k - the cash is not earmarked, so the THX trap is absent. Net cash reconciles to the filer exactly: cash GBP 17,390k, zero borrowings, IFRS-16 leases GBP 2,148k, net GBP 15,242k. What DOES fail is the screen's headline attraction: the 7.99% FCF yield is a working-capital artifact. FY26 free cash flow of GBP 10.0M contains a GBP 9.3M planned inventory release and excludes GBP 6.7M of capex paid in FY25; the company's own two-year figures are FY25 -GBP 7.7M and FY26 +GBP 10.0M, and ex-working-capital FY26 FCF is GBP 3.3M = a 2.5% yield. The screen's wc_fcf flag should have fired and did not. On the business: EBIT is the European heavy-truck cycle and nothing else. Registrations peaked at 344k in 2023 and Volvo estimates 310k for 2026; the company's despatch weight ex-Ductile went 53,100t -> 50,450t -> 40,100t -> 40,017t, and FY24->FY25 revenue -GBP 47.4M drove EBIT -GBP 15.0M, a 31.6% incremental drop-through. The FY26 'doubling' of EBIT sits on flat like-for-like volume and is mostly a GBP 1.5M electricity-penalty non-repeat, a GBP 1.3M Ductile loss reversal and a GBP 1.179M RDEC credit of which only GBP 0.4M recurs. So 11.6x EV/EBIT at 9.1% ROCE is a cycle-position statement, not a value statement. Utilisation is 41,500t sold against ~80,000t of sales capacity (52%), so the operating leverage into a real European recovery is genuine and the capex is already spent - that is the bull case, and it is worth ~420p. But you are being asked to pay for it at 300p after a +46% run. Concentration is severe and honestly disclosed: commercial vehicle 71% of revenue, top-4 customers 63%, largest 27%. Structurally, the company itself discloses that c.30% of revenue is cast-iron powertrain content exposed to electrification - a 2030s fuse, currently running the other way as US and EU emissions-target deferrals extend diesel HDV lifecycles. Register risk is the inverse of what a 190-year-old family-sounding foundry suggests: there is no control block, but Threadneedle, Aberforth, Ruffer and Janus Henderson hold ~48% of a stock that trades $87k a day, and both covering 'analysts' are the company's own joint house brokers.
